Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 24-Dec-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  Computational Neuroscience [NPT_4130]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                       Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Explain the role of neuron morphology in determining neural connectivity and function.                  (5)  
  
  
  A)                                                       Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  B)           Describe how systems of neurons collaborate to produce sensory-motor coordination.                      (5)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
2)                Discuss the ionic basis of membrane potential and the role of sodium-potassium channels in              (5)  
  generating action potentials.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Formulate the Hodgkin-Huxley model and explain how it captures the excitable membrane behavior (5)  
  of a neuron.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)                Compare the Hodgkin-Huxley model and the Morris-Lecar model in terms of complexity and                  (5)  
  applications.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Analyse phase-plane trajectories to interpret how changes in system parameters influence stability      (5)  
  and bifurcation behavior in neural models.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4)                Analyse how receptive field models and spike-triggered averaging techniques reveal stimulus-            (5)  
  response relationships in neurons and interpret their role in modelling neural activity.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Apply spike train distance measures to neural data and demonstrate how they can be used for             (5)  
  discrimination between different stimuli.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5)                Analyse how different forms of short-term plasticity influence temporal filtering and interpret their   (5)  
  implications for synaptic information processing.  
  
  Page #1

A)                                                              Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)                Evaluate computational models of long-term plasticity and their implications for adaptive neural     (5)  
  computation.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"
